page: Microsoft Azure FX24-6ms_v2 is a memory-dense virtual machine architecture configured with a low core-to-memory ratio and high base clock speeds. Virtualized under Microsoft Hyper-V on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 6 vCPUs derived from 3 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware subsystem incorporates a substantial 260 MB L3 cache along with native support for advanced vector and matrix instructions, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8. Memory allocation is exceptionally high at 504.0 GB total RAM, yielding an allocation of 84.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains zero local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of network-based storage volumes, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core efficiency alongside modest parallel throughput. The 4.2 GHz clock rate drives top-tier performance on the Geekbench single-core benchmark (2237.0) and Geekbench text processing (2928.0), both ranking within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Single-threaded data handling is reinforced by high compression marks, reaching 34.87 GB/sec in gzip and 14.4 GB/sec in bzip3 tests. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput scales moderately, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 6780.0 and stress-ng multi-core recording 6658.27, reflecting the physical limit of its 3-core footprint. Uncached memory access represents a measurable bottleneck, as 256 MB read bandwidth is categorized as weak at 35.26 GB/sec, while cached 16 KB read throughput registers at 518.22 GB/sec.

The qualitative efficiency profile of this instance hinges on memory-to-core licensing economics. For enterprise environments where software is billed per physical core or vCPU, the high ratio of 84.0 GB per core allows users to run vast working datasets while minimizing per-core software costs. However, workloads requiring massive parallel processing or high sequential memory transfer rates across uncached regions may find the limited core count restrictive. The platform is best suited for large in-memory databases, memory-constrained electronic design automation (EDA), heavy single-threaded computational tasks, and relational database systems with expansive caching tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24-6ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads that demand elevated CPU clock speeds. Provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 6 vCPUs across 3 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. It provides an exceptional memory capacity of 504.0 GB RAM, yielding 84.0 GB per vCPU, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, AMX matrix acceleration, and AVX-512 instruction sets. Local storage is absent, requiring external persistent disks, and no GPUs are attached. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core compute and text processing scores alongside high single-threaded compression rates, while uncached memory bandwidth and multi-core scaling remain moderate. The hardware profile is optimal for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation, financial analytics, and memory-bound transactional services requiring low per-core software licensing footprints.
